title: X Feed Digest
summary: AI workflow shift: The feed centered on how AI is changing real work, from OpenAI's rare-disease research and Google's Gemini interview pilot to posts arguing that prompt placement and tool choice matter more than generic vibe coding.
Macro risk: Iran and the Strait of Hormuz stayed in focus, with market posts treating shipping disruption and Middle East tension as live inputs for energy and risk assets.
Football overload: The rest of the timeline was dominated by World Cup and international football clips, especially first goals, viral reactions, and Lamine Yamal chatter.
Broad market tone: Sector commentary stayed constructive, with cyclicals leading while defensives and gold miners lagged.

items.title: @OpenAI: o3 Deep Research in clinical care
items.body: OpenAI highlighted a NEJM AI study with Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard showing o3 Deep Research helping clinicians revisit unsolved rare pediatric disease cases. The signal is less about a benchmark and more about AI becoming useful in real clinical triage and literature review.

items.title: @Xudong07452910: Google tests Gemini in interviews
items.body: Google is reportedly piloting Gemini in parts of software engineering interviews, reflecting a shift from banning AI in assessment to treating it as part of the job. The post argues the real skill is now using AI to build, verify, and debug software.

items.title: @VincentLogic: Karpathy's prompt workflow
items.body: Karpathy's advice here is that long natural-language prompts are less efficient than putting the cursor on the right line and letting the model complete from local context. The takeaway is that AI coding quality depends heavily on where and how you supply context.

items.title: @mylifcc: GLM-5.2 edges Claude Fable 5
items.body: This post summarizes a model-vs-model result claiming GLM-5.2 topped a single-turn web design benchmark, with lower cost and MIT licensing. The interesting part is the explanation: layout awareness, Tailwind-heavy output, and stronger above-the-fold design made it win on user preference.

items.title: @WatcherGuru: Trump on the Strait of Hormuz
items.body: Trump said there would be no tolls in the Strait of Hormuz unless imposed by and for the United States, keeping the shipping lane and Iran dispute front and center for energy markets.

items.title: @Liv_Boeree: Hormuz closure chatter
items.body: A widely shared repost claimed the Strait of Hormuz was closed over the weekend with limited operating windows starting Monday. Even as a social post rather than a formal bulletin, it shows how quickly the market is repricing geopolitical risk.

items.title: @NateSilver538: Iran conflict grinds on
items.body: Silver's read is blunt: the confrontation has become a real quagmire against Iran. That kind of framing tends to matter because it feeds expectations about duration, escalation, and policy response.

items.title: @WallStCourier: Cyclicals still leading
items.body: The sector note says the market remains constructive, with Industrials and Financials in very strong trend regimes while Health Care, Consumer Staples, and gold miners lag. The message is that risk appetite is still tilted toward cyclicals.

items.title: @TheAroraReport: Mania can outlast caution
items.body: A short market quote warns that AI, space, and options manias can last longer than expected, but asks whether investors are positioned for the turn. It is a simple reminder that momentum and risk can stay extended.

items.title: @FabrizioRomano: Endrick puts the team first
items.body: Endrick is quoted saying Ancelotti will do what is best for the team, not for individual players or fan wishes. It is a standard squad-selection quote, but it also signals the pressure around Real Madrid's lineup decisions.

items.title: @heis_fede: Japan coach stunned by goal four
items.body: The clip captures Japan's coach reacting to his side scoring a fourth goal against Tunisia. It is the kind of viral sports moment that spread the fastest in this feed.

items.title: @FOXSports: Raul Jimenez's emotional World Cup moment
items.body: FOX framed Raul Jimenez's first World Cup goal as a tribute moment, with Thierry Henry highlighting the emotional weight of honoring his late father. It was one of the clearest human-interest posts in the timeline.

items.title: @TouchlineX: Lamine Yamal on Messi-level longevity
items.body: Yamal says playing until 40 at Messi's level is basically impossible and says he misses watching players people genuinely enjoy. The quote is notable because it shows how he frames football as entertainment and craft, not just results.

items.title: @FOXSports: Seattle's first USMNT World Cup night
items.body: FOX highlighted the first World Cup match in Seattle for the USMNT, with Trinity Rodman bringing out the match ball and Alex Freeman's goal making it 2-0 after VAR review. The feed made it clear the home crowd angle mattered.
